description: Implementation map for applying every template context field to generated repository artifacts.

statuses.external: Consumed by callers or Cookiecutter routing rather than rendered into files.
statuses.control: Controls whether files or directories are included.
statuses.implemented: Currently rendered into generated project artifacts.
statuses.partial: Currently rendered, but additional relevant artifacts are planned.
statuses.planned: Represented in the contract and reserved for future artifacts.

fields.name: language
fields.notes: Used by APIs and other callers to choose the template directory; also used by post-generation compatibility checks.

fields.name: project_name
fields.notes: Rendered into public project titles, citation metadata, and CodeMeta metadata.

fields.name: project_slug
fields.notes: Used wherever the machine-readable project name is required. The contract and generation hook apply language-specific package-name constraints.

fields.name: project_short_description
fields.notes: Short public package description and fallback text for richer metadata.

fields.name: project_long_description
fields.notes: Rendered as optional public motivation and scope prose, with the short description used as a fallback.

fields.name: version
fields.notes: Initial package version. Sphinx derives its displayed release from installed package metadata. The Python template checks generated metadata surfaces for consistency.

fields.name: development_status
fields.notes: Controlled repostatus.org lifecycle status for machine-readable metadata.

fields.name: keywords
fields.notes: Useful for machine-readable discovery metadata.

fields.name: authors
fields.notes: Multiple authors are supported in pyproject.toml, CITATION.cff, and CodeMeta. CodeMeta entries use stable identifiers when ORCID or URL values are provided.

fields.name: maintainers
fields.notes: Rendered as package maintainer metadata, CITATION.cff contact metadata, and CodeMeta maintainer metadata. CodeMeta entries use stable identifiers when ORCID or URL values are provided.

fields.name: principal_investigators
fields.notes: Public project leadership metadata. CodeMeta entries use stable identifiers when ORCID or URL values are provided.

fields.name: organization_name
fields.notes: Rendered in Python Sphinx configuration, CodeMeta provider metadata, and citation/CodeMeta fallback authors when no authors are provided.

fields.name: funding
fields.notes: Multiple public funding records are rendered as CodeMeta funder/funding metadata and a readable docs overview section.

fields.name: purpose
fields.notes: Public purpose statement rendered in human-facing project context.

fields.name: purpose_categories
fields.notes: Public purpose categories rendered in human-facing project context.

fields.name: audiences
fields.notes: Intended audiences rendered in human-facing project context.

fields.name: related_software
fields.notes: Related software is rendered as public context and machine-readable CodeMeta relatedLink values when names or links are provided.

fields.name: repository_url
fields.notes: Rendered into package metadata, source citation metadata, CodeMeta metadata, generated docs configuration, and metadata validation.

fields.name: homepage_url
fields.notes: Rendered as the preferred public landing page when provided.

fields.name: documentation_url
fields.notes: Rendered as documentation metadata and a README link when distinct from the repository and homepage URLs.

fields.name: registries
fields.notes: Registry entries render as machine-readable identifiers. Represented in CFF identifiers as type other with the registry name as the description.

fields.name: persistent_identifiers
fields.notes: Supports the CFF identifier types DOI, URL, SWH, and other. CodeMeta contains an explicit replacement placeholder until a persistent identifier is supplied.

fields.name: publications
fields.notes: Associated publications render into concise public notes plus CFF references and CodeMeta referencePublication. A publication marked preferred becomes the CFF preferred-citation and public note.

fields.name: license
fields.notes: SPDX identifiers are fetched for the generated license file and rendered into machine metadata. Empty values omit the license file. Unrecognized values are written as custom license text.

fields.name: license_compatibility_notes
fields.notes: Public compatibility notes only.

fields.name: license_compatibility_check
targets: Python dependency license compatibility CI workflow
fields.notes: Binary switch for generated dependency license compatibility checking. Python uses licensecheck through a dedicated CI workflow when CI and a recognized SPDX license are present.

fields.name: include_citation_cff
fields.notes: Controls CFF citation metadata. The LUMC profile workflow is included when its required CFF file is present.

fields.name: documentation_builder
fields.notes: Language-specific defaults are defined in the context contract. Python selects Sphinx or MkDocs scaffolds, docs extras, and docs CI build commands, and uses the Python default when an incompatible builder is requested. R consumes the field but still needs the pkgdown scaffold.

fields.name: documentation_types
fields.notes: The SMP-aligned user, deployment, and developer values drive docs inclusion and page selection. Developer documentation includes technical and API reference material. Empty entries remove the docs scaffold.

fields.name: include_contributing
fields.notes: Binary switch for including the standard contributing guide scaffold and pull request template.

fields.name: include_code_of_conduct
fields.notes: Binary switch for including the standard code of conduct scaffold.

fields.name: include_governance
fields.notes: Binary switch for including the standard governance scaffold.

fields.name: include_security
fields.notes: Binary switch for including the standard security policy scaffold.

fields.name: include_support
fields.notes: Binary switch for including the standard support scaffold and structured GitHub issue forms.

fields.name: include_changelog
fields.notes: Binary switch for including the standard changelog scaffold and deterministic Keep a Changelog format check.

fields.name: support_routes
fields.notes: Multiple public support or issue-reporting systems and URLs, matching the SMP list shape. The first public URL is used as the package issue URL.

fields.name: code_of_conduct_contact
fields.notes: Public private-contact route for code-of-conduct reports.

fields.name: governance_notes
fields.notes: Public governance and decision-making notes.

fields.name: programming_languages
fields.notes: Should include language, version constraint, and role.

fields.name: software_functions
fields.notes: Links public EDAM operations to inputs, outputs, command examples, and notes. Function inputs and outputs are the canonical source for data and format metadata.

fields.name: interfaces
fields.notes: Controlled public tool types describe how users access the software and select minimal Python scaffolds for common interface families. Specification and status are rendered in project documentation; status does not suppress a requested scaffold.

fields.name: operating_systems
fields.notes: Documents all declared platform support. Officially supported Python platforms also render into package classifiers and the tests CI matrix when they map to GitHub-hosted runners; both SMP statuses are represented in CodeMeta.

fields.name: external_dependencies
fields.notes: Public external requirements beyond normal language package metadata. Entries render into human-readable docs and CodeMeta softwareRequirements.

fields.name: external_services
fields.notes: Public external services, partners, or roles needed by the project. Entries render into generated documentation only.

fields.name: test_types
fields.notes: SMP checklist labels control test inclusion and which generated sample tests are kept. Empty entries omit the test suite and its CI workflow. Python currently renders pytest-compatible sample tests.

fields.name: test_frameworks
fields.notes: Controlled framework names with template-specific supported choices. Python currently supports pytest and keeps pytest commands and dependencies.

fields.name: formatter_tool
fields.notes: One controlled formatter choice. Python currently supports ruff.

fields.name: linter_tool
fields.notes: One controlled linter choice. Python currently supports ruff.

fields.name: type_checker
fields.notes: Controlled tool names with template-specific supported choices. Python currently supports mypy as an opt-in type checker.

fields.name: project_manager
fields.notes: One controlled primary manager with template-specific choices and defaults. Python supports uv, Poetry, PDM, Hatch, Pixi, and pip; uv is the default. Hatchling remains the independent Python build backend.

fields.name: versioning_scheme
fields.notes: Documents the project policy and drives Python release validation when a recognized scheme is selected.

fields.name: versioning_scheme_details
fields.notes: Preserves an exact CalVer pattern or a public custom versioning policy.

fields.name: release_frequency
fields.notes: Public release cadence expectation.

fields.name: distribution_channels
fields.notes: Python automates PyPI, GitHub Releases, GitHub Container Registry, and Docker Hub paths; other destinations are documented for their external setup.

fields.name: containerization
fields.notes: Python generates Docker, OCI/Podman, and Apptainer/Singularity recipes. Project managers and their lockfiles are controlled independently.

fields.name: resource_requirements
targets: README fallback when docs are omitted
fields.notes: Public typical and worst-case memory, storage, compute, GPU, wall-clock, and scaling expectations.

fields.name: maintenance_level
fields.notes: Controlled public support and maintenance commitment after active development.

fields.name: continuity_plan
fields.notes: Public handover or continuity notes.

fields.name: retirement_criteria
fields.notes: Public criteria for archival or retirement.

fields.name: public_risk_notes
fields.notes: Public risk notes only; sensitive detail belongs elsewhere.

fields.name: security_contact
fields.notes: Public private-contact route for vulnerability reports.

fields.name: security_measures
fields.notes: Public security measures such as access control, patch management, vulnerability scanning, network controls, or institutional policies.

fields.name: additional_security_measures
fields.notes: Public free-text complement to the controlled security measures list.

fields.name: sensitive_data_statement
fields.notes: Public data-handling statement without restricted details.

fields.name: dmp_reference
fields.notes: Public DMP reference or contact route when appropriate.
